texts: good. fires as a rule once per molting, with the feathers falling to the cliff's base during that molt and the base correctly recorded as part of the cliff.

good. as clean as your first text: "the sky-cat" ties back to the molting cat, the shedding is a per-occasion event linked to the molt, and "onto the base of the cliff" is read as where the feathers end up.

good. parses as a habitual rule per apprentice — each collects, in the morning, the specific batch of fallen feathers, with "fallen" handed down to each feather in that batch rather than asserted of the batch as an object.

bad: "the Keepers" was turned into an untyped group of keepers with no name recorded at all, so the storer has no identity in the result, and the extra per-member rule then ranges over members the name never licensed (the adjudicator confirmed all three points). The sentence itself is fine if the Keepers act as one body — the same label parsed cleanly in "The Keepers tolerate sky-cats" — but if you mean each of them does the storing, say so outright: "Each Keeper stores the collected feathers in a bin at the Watch."
